title: Cap. VIII: Corvinus with Arminius — reprobation only from personal rejection of offered grace
pass_a_gloss: He therefore with Arminius establishes that God always reprobates singular persons from their own personal rejection of offered grace; so that neither in the decree of reprobation has he rejected or passed by anyone except considered as actually unbelieving and impenitent against God actually calling, nor in the fall of Adam has he left anyone from his absolute ordination, or decreed to damn on account of original sin alone.
pass_b_english: With Arminius he therefore holds this: God always reprobates particular persons from their own personal rejection of offered grace. In the reprobation decree, on that view, he has rejected or passed by no one except as actually unbelieving and impenitent against God who is actually calling. Nor in Adam's fall has he left anyone by absolute ordination alone, or decreed to damn for original sin only.
source_text: Is igitur cum Arminio statuit, Deum singulares personas semper reprobare ex personali earundem propria gratiae oblatae rejectione; ita ut nec in decreto reprobationis quenquam rejecerit aut praeterierit nisi consideratum ut actu infidelem et impenitentem contra Deum actu vocantem, nec in Adae lapsu quenquam ex absoluta sua ordinatione reliquerit, aut propter solum originale peccatum damnare decreverit.
